fix(chat): agent switch cleanup order — always cleanup before multi-agent check

setCurrentAgent now calls cleanupAgent(prev) BEFORE checking multi-agent
session reuse. Previously, cleanup was deferred to the non-multi-agent
path, allowing Agent A's StreamSession to continue writing events while
Agent B was displayed — causing "previous agent's chat persists" bug.

Order change:
  OLD: multi-agent check → conditional cleanupAgent
  NEW: cleanupAgent(prev) → update(prev, connectionPhase:idle) → m

fix(extract): role detector tests FIRST CLAUSE not full message

The universal-rule role detector required 8..120 codepoints over the
WHOLE message. Real-world persona prompts (e.g. tests/pi-extension.test.ts
'You are a senior staff engineer. <500 chars of context>') exceeded
this cap and were never classified as role.

Switch the structural test to the first clause (split on .!\n。！) — the
sentence boundary that delimits 'You are X' across English, French
('Tu es X.'), Japanese ('あなたは X です。'), S

fix(setup-center): respect backend ownership during startup, kill all on quit

The Tauri shell was unconditionally terminating any backend it
discovered on the API port, which meant a manually launched
`python -m openakita serve` would be killed the moment a dev
build of the desktop app started up. The auto-replace logic
served release upgrades but treated every external process as an
old packaged backend, with no way to opt out.

Introduce an ownership-aware policy backed by the `started_by`
fi

## Summary
After `openshell inference set` swaps the gateway's inference provider
entry, `agents.defaults.model.primary` in `openclaw.json` can drift from
`models.providers.<key>.models[0].id`. The gateway then routes requests
to the new model but the OpenClaw agent self-reports the old one. This
change reconciles the two on every sandbox start so the agent boots with
a consistent identity.
